tickets.title: PR 2: Privileged helper and local channel for approved commands
tickets.body:
## Goal
Privileged work runs in a separate helper process, never in the unprivileged agent. The helper runs only commands that carry a valid Core-signed operator approval (from the approval-gate ticket), over a local authenticated channel. This ticket closes the privileged-execution prerequisite in `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` (forward plan item 3). It depends on the approval gate and on transcript retention, so K-3, K-5 and K-6 (which depend on K-2) start only once all three pieces have landed.

## Current state (master `f9c8b7f`)
- The agent runs unprivileged: a Windows virtual service account, or a dedicated systemd user with a watchdog (`cmd/nerve-agent/service_windows.go`, `service_linux.go`, `scripts/agent/`).
- `internal/remote/policy.go` lists only read-only command types. Privileged capabilities have no policy and are refused.
- Command claim, start and result go through signed agent endpoints (`internal/httpapi/commands.go`).

## Changes
1. **Decision record** `docs/DECISIONS/0003-privileged-helper.md`: process split, the local channel, why the helper cannot reach Core itself, and the threat model (a compromised agent account must not be able to run arbitrary privileged code).
2. **Helper.** A `nerve-agent helper` mode installed as a second service: LocalSystem on Windows, a root systemd unit on Linux with a minimal `CapabilityBoundingSet`. `service install` gains a `--with-helper` flag. The default stays without a helper.
3. **Local channel.** Windows: a named pipe whose DACL allows only the agent's virtual account. Linux: a Unix socket in a root-owned directory, with the peer UID checked through `SO_PEERCRED`. Each request carries the full approval envelope. The helper verifies the Core signature with the pinned Core key, checks expiry, binding to this agent and device, and single use, then dispatches to a handler registry. The registry stays empty in this ticket apart from a test-only no-op.
4. **Agent.** For a privileged command type, the agent forwards to the helper instead of executing it, and reports `helper_unavailable` as a failure when no helper is installed. It advertises privileged capabilities only when the helper answers a signed health check.
5. **Diagnose.** `nerve-agent diagnose` reports helper status and channel permissions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Helper refuses: a missing, expired, replayed or tampered approval; an approval for another agent or device; a caller other than the agent account (Windows and Linux tests)
- [ ] With no helper installed, privileged commands fail closed and the capability is not advertised
- [ ] Linux systemd end-to-end run with the helper; `GOOS=windows` build and Windows-native tests; install and uninstall scripts updated
- [ ] Decision record 0003; security review; `REMOTE_MANAGEMENT.md`, `AGENT_SETUP.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` updated; CI green

tickets.title: Authenticate the discovery worker with its enrolled agent identity
tickets.body:
## Goal
The discovery worker inside `nerve-agent` authenticates to Core with the agent's enrolled Ed25519 identity, the same one management already uses, instead of the shared `NERVE_DISCOVERY_AGENT_TOKEN` bearer token. A discovery report is then attributable to one revocable agent and cannot be sent by anyone who only read `.env`.

## Current state (origin/master `f9c8b7f`)
- Discovery routes `POST /api/v1/discovery/agent/{heartbeat,jobs/claim,jobs/{scanID}/report,jobs/{scanID}/complete}` (`internal/httpapi/server.go`) are guarded by `requireDiscoveryAgent` (`internal/httpapi/discovery.go`): constant-time compare against `cfg.DiscoveryAgentToken`.
- The worker's identity is the self-asserted header `X-NERVE-Agent-ID`, built as `hostname + "-" + GOOS` (`cmd/nerve-agent/main.go` `newDiscoveryAgent`). Any token holder can pose as any discovery agent.
- `discovery_agents.id` is free `text`; `discovery_scans.agent_id` references it (`migrations/000003_local_discovery.up.sql`).
- Management requests already go through `agentEndpoint` (`internal/httpapi/agents.go`): signed headers, `agents.Repository.Authenticate` (signature, revocation, nonce replay, clock skew), Core-signed responses verified against the pinned Core key (`cmd/nerve-agent/management.go` `signedPost`).
- `runAgent` (`cmd/nerve-agent/cli.go`) starts the discovery worker only when `NERVE_DISCOVERY_AGENT_TOKEN` is set, independently of enrollment.

## Changes
1. **Capability.** Add `discovery.scan` (read-only risk; it sends ARP/ICMP/TCP probes only to the administrator-configured target) to `agentproto.Catalogue`. An enrolled agent reports it in its heartbeat when the discovery worker is enabled on that host.
2. **Core routes.** Wrap the four discovery agent routes in `agentEndpoint` with suitable body limits (the report route needs the current report size). The handler takes the agent identity from the authenticated `Principal`, never from a header. Refuse with 403 when the agent does not currently report `discovery.scan`.
3. **Schema.** New ordered migration `000011_discovery_agent_identity`: add `discovery_agents.agent_id uuid NULL REFERENCES agents(id)` (unique when set). Enrolled workers upsert their row keyed by agent id; legacy text rows stay readable so scan history is kept. Do not edit `000003`.
4. **Agent.** When the agent is enrolled, the discovery worker reuses the management identity, transport (private-CA TLS) and `signedPost` with Core-response verification. Enable it with an explicit setting in the agent `config.json` (for example `"discovery": true`) rather than with the presence of a token.
5. **Migration path.**
   - Enrolled + discovery enabled: signed path; the shared token is ignored and a warning is logged if it is still set.
   - Not enrolled + token set: legacy bearer path keeps working, with a deprecation warning in the agent log and on the Discovery page ("worker uses the deprecated shared token, enroll it").
   - New Core setting `NERVE_DISCOVERY_LEGACY_TOKEN` (default enabled for this release) lets an operator switch the bearer path off. Removing it entirely is a later release, noted in `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
   - `scripts/manage-discovery-agent.ps1`, `start.example.bat` and `setup.ps1` keep working unchanged for existing installs; document how to enroll the local worker instead.
6. **Audit.** Signed discovery heartbeats and reports record `actor_agent_id` where scan state changes, like management commands.

## Out of scope
- The Windows traffic sensor (separate ticket, needs a .NET signing decision).
- Idempotent report ingestion (a known limitation, its own ticket).
- Key rotation (K-10).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Discovery routes accept signed requests from an enrolled agent that reports `discovery.scan`, and refuse unsigned, replayed, revoked or capability-less requests (integration tests against PostgreSQL)
- [ ] Scan claims and reports record the enrolled agent id from the signature; a client-supplied agent id header is ignored on the signed path
- [ ] The legacy bearer path still works when enabled, can be turned off with `NERVE_DISCOVERY_LEGACY_TOKEN=false`, and logs a deprecation warning
- [ ] Migration `000011` applies to a database with existing legacy discovery rows and keeps scan history
- [ ] Agent unit tests: the worker uses the signed client when enrolled and verifies Core's response signature
- [ ] Security review of the change (authentication and ingestion)
- [ ] `AGENT_SETUP.md`, `REMOTE_MANAGEMENT.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` updated; `go test ./...`, `go vet`, integration tests and CI green

tickets.title: Match Traffic Map flows to devices by any current address
tickets.body:
## Goal
A flow whose local address is any current address of an inventory device is attributed to that device in the Traffic Map. Today only the device's primary address counts, so traffic from secondary addresses shows up as an unidentified "observed" host.

## Current state (origin/master `f9c8b7f`)
- `components/map/topology.ts` `buildTopology` builds `localByIP` from `device.primaryIpAddress` only. Flows whose `localIp` is not in it become `host:<ip>` observed nodes. The "traffic" device filter checks only the primary address. When several devices claim the same address, `preferred` picks the online, most recently seen one.
- `components/map/use-device-inventory.ts` pages through `GET /api/v1/devices`. `DeviceSummary` (`internal/inventory/models.go`, `lib/types.ts`) carries only `primaryIpAddress`, which is derived in `internal/inventory/devices.go` from `ip_addresses` / `interface_addresses` (`valid_until IS NULL` means current).
- `npm run test:map` runs `scripts/check-topology-layout.mjs`, which builds devices with a single `primaryIpAddress`.

## Changes
1. **API.** Add `ipAddresses: string[]` to `DeviceSummary`: all current addresses (`valid_until IS NULL`), deduplicated, primary first, capped (for example at 16) to keep list pages bounded. Compute it with one aggregated subquery in the list query, not a query per device. Update `lib/types.ts`.
2. **Topology.** Index every current address of each device in `localByIP`, keeping the existing `preferred` rule for conflicts. The rule applies per address, so a device can win one address and lose another. The "traffic" filter and the observed-only suppression (`inventoryIPs`) use all addresses. The node label and `ip` stay the primary address. The node detail lists the matched addresses.
3. **Honest provenance.** Only current addresses are used. Addresses with `valid_until` set never attract traffic, so an old lease cannot attribute today's traffic to the wrong device.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `check-topology-layout.mjs` covers: a flow on a secondary address joins the device, the conflict rule applies per address, the traffic filter keeps a device whose only active address is secondary, and no observed node appears for a secondary address
- [ ] Go test for the list query: only current addresses, primary first, capped
- [ ] `npm run test:map`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `go test ./...` and integration tests pass
- [ ] Checked in a browser with the review stack (signed test-sensor feed) at desktop and narrow widths

tickets.title: PR 7: Versioned, signed agent releases
tickets.body:
## Goal
NERVE starts versioning. A tag builds Windows and Linux agent artifacts, signs a release manifest and publishes a GitHub release with a changelog. The agent can verify a release offline against a pinned release key. This is the foundation for remote updates, which come in a separate ticket.

## Current state (master `f9c8b7f`)
- `cmd/nerve-agent/main.go` has `var version = "dev"`. `Dockerfile.agent` sets it via `-X main.version=${NERVE_VERSION}`.
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) builds Windows and Linux agent artifacts (`--target artifact`) and the sensor, but nothing is published. There are no tags, no releases and no changelog.
- `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` forward plan item 9 asks for versioning to start as soon as agents ship.

## Changes
1. **Decision record** `docs/DECISIONS/` for the release signing scheme. Options: an Ed25519 release key reusing `agentproto` primitives, with the private key held only as a GitHub Actions secret in a protected `release` environment; or Sigstore/cosign keyless signing. Prefer Ed25519, because the agent must verify offline without a Sigstore client. Record how the key is generated, rotated and revoked.
2. **Versioning.** SemVer tags `vX.Y.Z`, `CHANGELOG.md` (Keep a Changelog format), and the version embedded in agent, API and web builds. `nerve-agent --version` prints it.
3. **Release workflow** `.github/workflows/release.yml`, triggered on tags in the protected environment. It builds agent artifacts for windows/amd64, linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 reproducibly (`-trimpath`, fixed `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`), writes `manifest.json` (version, per-file SHA-256, minimum Core version), signs it, adds SPDX SBOMs, and creates a GitHub release with the changelog section.
4. **Agent verification library.** `internal/release` provides `VerifyManifest(pinnedKeys, manifest, signature)` and `VerifyArtifact(manifest, file)`. The release public key ships compiled into the agent; a list allows a future rotation. Add a `nerve-agent verify-release <dir>` command.
5. **Docs.** `CONTRIBUTING`/`docs/WORKFLOW.md`: how to cut a release.

## Out of scope
The remote update command and rollback (separate ticket, needs the privileged helper from K-2).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tag dry run on a fork or with `workflow_dispatch` produces signed artifacts, a manifest, SBOMs and a release draft
- [ ] `internal/release` tests: valid, tampered manifest, tampered artifact, unknown key, wrong platform
- [ ] Two builds of the same tag produce identical artifact hashes
- [ ] Decision record; `CHANGELOG.md` started at the first version; CI green

notes.author: claude
notes.text: Maintainer decision (2026-10-22): releases via GitHub tags and GitHub Releases; Ed25519 signing key as a secret in a protected GitHub environment.

tickets.title: Offline vendor (OUI) lookup for observed MAC addresses
tickets.body:
## Goal
Core resolves the vendor of each observed MAC address from a bundled, offline OUI table. The result is stored as a sourced device attribute. Observed MAC addresses never leave the installation.

## Current state (origin/master `f9c8b7f`)
- Sourced claims live in `device_attributes` and are written with `devices.RecordAttribute` (`internal/devices/attributes.go`). `RefreshDiscovered` copies the most confident claim per attribute into the discovered columns, including `manufacturer`. Operator-owned fields are never touched.
- Inventory already exposes and sorts by `vendor`, read from `devices.manufacturer` (`internal/inventory/devices.go`). Today only agent facts fill it, so most discovered devices show no vendor.
- Discovery reconciliation creates and updates devices in `internal/discovery/repository.go`.

## Changes
1. **Data source (decision record).** Choose the table and record its licence in `docs/DECISIONS/` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`. Candidates are the IEEE MA-L/MA-M/MA-S registries (public CSV) and Wireshark's `manuf` (GPL-2.0). The repository has no licence file yet, so prefer the IEEE data unless the decision says otherwise. Ship a compact generated file embedded with `go:embed` in a new `internal/oui` package. Add a `scripts/` generator that downloads and normalises the registry, so updating is a reviewed PR and never a runtime download.
2. **Lookup.** `oui.Lookup(mac)` does longest-prefix matching over MA-S (36 bit), MA-M (28 bit) and MA-L (24 bit). It returns no vendor for locally administered addresses (bit 0x02 of the first octet set, which covers randomised phone MACs) and for multicast addresses.
3. **Recording.** When discovery or an agent reports a MAC for a device, record `manufacturer` with source `oui` and a confidence below `ConfidenceAgent` (for example 40), so an enrolled agent's own claim wins. Add a one-off backfill for existing interfaces, either at startup or as a migration-driven job; it must be idempotent.
4. **UI.** The device detail evidence list shows the `oui` source like other provenance entries. No new screen.

## Out of scope
Automatic device classification (separate ticket that builds on this one).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decision record for the data source and its licence; notices updated
- [ ] Unit tests: MA-L/MA-M/MA-S precedence, locally administered and multicast addresses, malformed input
- [ ] Integration test: a discovered device gains `manufacturer` from `oui`, and an agent-reported manufacturer still wins
- [ ] No network access at runtime (the lookup table is embedded); the generator script is documented
- [ ] `go test ./...`, `go vet`, integration tests and CI green; `ARCHITECTURE.md` updated

notes.author: claude
notes.text:
Implemented on k-11/oui-lookup (3 commits, not pushed).
- `internal/oui`: embedded IEEE MA-L/MA-M/MA-S table (`registry.tsv`, 53,621 prefixes, 1.6 MB, retrieved 2026-10-23) with longest-prefix lookup. Multicast and locally administered addresses never resolve. The generator `scripts/generate-oui.mjs` drops organization addresses, "Private" entries and blocks held as "IEEE Registration Authority", so an unassigned sub-block finds no vendor.
- `devices.RecordVendor` records `manufacturer`, source `oui`, confidence 40. It is called from discovery reconciliation and from agent evidence sync. A MAC seen by discovery is preferred over agent-only adapters. `devices.BackfillVendors` runs once at Core startup for live devices with a MAC and no `oui` claim; it is idempotent.
- UI: no change needed, because the Identity tab already lists every fact source.
- Docs: decision 0004, new `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, DEVICE_IDENTITY, ARCHITECTURE, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN and README updated.
- Verified in Docker (golang:1.27, postgres:17): gofmt, go vet (with and without the integration tag, plus GOOS=windows for the agent), unit tests and all integration tests pass. New integration tests cover the discovery path, agent precedence, backfill and randomized MACs, plus the agent-MAC path. The API image builds. The agent binary links no `oui` symbols, so its size is unchanged.
- For the maintainer: the IEEE CSV files carry no licence statement (see decision 0004). Please confirm that is acceptable. Lookups still return an assigned vendor for a device that has a virtual NIC.

tickets.title: Automatic device classification as a sourced fact
tickets.body:
## Goal
Suggest a device classification (workstation, printer, router, ...) from observed evidence, stored with source and confidence. An operator's classification override always wins.

## Current state (origin/master `f9c8b7f`)
- `devices.classification` is set to `'unknown'` when discovery creates a device (`internal/discovery/repository.go`). The operator override lives in `classification_override` with the vocabulary `devices.Classifications` (`internal/devices/metadata.go`).
- Sourced claims go through `device_attributes` / `RecordAttribute` / `RefreshDiscovered` (`internal/devices/attributes.go`). `classification` is not yet one of the `discoveredColumns`.
- Evidence available: OUI vendor (after K-11), open services from discovery, agent host facts (OS, run mode), hostname.

## Changes
1. Add `classification` to `discoveredColumns`, so the discovered value follows the most confident claim and the override still takes precedence in inventory.
2. Add a small rule table in a new `internal/devices/classify.go`: each rule has inputs (vendor pattern, service ports, agent OS) and produces a classification from the existing vocabulary with a confidence and a human-readable reason. No machine learning and no external lookups.
3. Record the result as attribute `classification` with source `heuristic` whenever the inputs change. Recompute for existing devices once.
4. The device detail page shows the suggested classification with its reason and confidence next to the override control.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Rules covered by table-driven unit tests, including conflicts between rules and "no rule matched" (stays `unknown`)
- [ ] Integration test: the operator override wins over the heuristic, and a cleared override falls back to it
- [ ] Reasons are visible in the UI; no classification is shown without its source
- [ ] `go test ./...`, integration tests, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build`; checked in a browser

notes.author: claude
notes.text:
Implemented on k-16/device-classification (2 commits, not pushed).
- `internal/devices/classify.go`: rule table over the effective manufacturer, the effective OS and open TCP ports in service_endpoints. Each rule gives a type from the vocabulary, a confidence (40–75) and a reason. The most confident rule wins; on a tie, the earlier rule. Vendors that make many kinds of devices (Cisco, HP, Apple, Microsoft) have no rule. Vendor patterns were checked against every matching IEEE name to avoid false hits such as "Brother, Brother & Sons", other "AVM" companies and Kyocera phones.
- Recording: source `heuristic`. It reruns when a manufacturer or operating_system claim changes (in `RecordAttribute`), after `ForgetSource`, and for all live devices at Core startup. When no rule matches any more, the claim is withdrawn and the type falls back to `unknown`. `classification` is now a discovered column; `ForgetSource` falls back to `unknown` for it because the column is NOT NULL.
- Migration 000012 adds 'classification' to the device_attributes attribute CHECK (required; the constraint rejected it). It is numbered 000012 because K-22 uses 000011. The ledger is keyed by filename, so both apply in either landing order.
- API and UI: the identity report carries `classification` (suggestion, source, confidence, reason). The Identity tab shows "type · source, confidence N" plus the reason, or "unknown · no rule matched". The reason is shown only while it still explains the effective claim.
- Verified: gofmt, go vet (with and without the integration tag, plus GOOS=windows for the agent), unit tests and all integration tests on PostgreSQL 17. The new integration test covers the heuristic, override wins, cleared override falls back, a stronger agent OS claim and ForgetSource, withdrawal and repeatable backfill. npm typecheck and build pass. Browser check on an isolated Compose stack (port 3816, test admin, seeded devices): printer, virtual_machine (VMware vendor beats the Windows client OS) and unknown (Cisco) all display correctly, including at 375 px width. The stack has been removed.
- Limits: port rules only fire once something records service_endpoints, which local discovery does not do yet. Laptops, phones and Linux hosts are not told apart.

tickets.title: Redaction and retention for remote command transcripts
tickets.body:
## Goal
Command output that will soon contain shell transcripts is redacted before it is stored and pruned after a defined retention period, so secrets do not accumulate in PostgreSQL.

## Current state (master `f9c8b7f`)
- `remote_command_results` (`migrations/000007_remote_commands.up.sql`) stores `output jsonb`, `stdout`, `stderr` (each up to 1 MiB), truncation flags and a `result_digest`. The comment says rows may be pruned by retention, but no retention exists.
- Result submission: `agentSubmitResult` (`internal/httpapi/commands.go`).

## Changes
1. **Redaction** in the agent before upload, with the same rules re-applied in Core: patterns for common secrets (bearer tokens, `password=`, private key blocks, AWS-style keys, connection strings with credentials). Replace matches with `[redacted:<kind>]` and record the count per kind in the result. Rules live in one shared Go package with table-driven tests. The digest covers the redacted text.
2. **Retention.** `NERVE_COMMAND_RESULT_RETENTION` (default 30 days). A periodic Core job deletes result rows older than that and keeps the command row and its audit entries. The UI shows "output removed by retention" instead of an empty result.
3. **Access.** Viewing stdout/stderr of privileged commands needs `RemoteExecutePrivileged` or a new view permission, not just `RemoteView`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Redaction unit tests with true and false positives; the digest is stable across agent and Core
- [ ] Integration test: retention prunes only expired results, and command history stays intact
- [ ] Documented in `REMOTE_MANAGEMENT.md`; the retention gap is removed from `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` known limitations; CI green

K-22 also changes internal/remote/commands.go. Notes for the implementer: retention needs no schema change, because "removed by retention" can be derived from a completed command without a result row. Access can use the existing authz.RemoteExecutePrivileged permission, which needs no migration either.

Use the next free number (000013; 000011 is K-22 and 000012 is K-16). K-22 only changes one error message in internal/remote/commands.go, so there is no real overlap.

tickets.title: Reusable deployment keys with operator approval of new agents
tickets.body:
## Goal
IT can enroll many endpoints with one deployment key instead of one single-use token per machine. The key is limited, revocable and optionally scoped. Agents that enroll with it wait for operator approval unless the key explicitly allows automatic acceptance.

## Current state (master `f9c8b7f`)
- Enrollment tokens (`nerve-enroll-v2.<enrollment id>.<secret>.<Core key fingerprint>`) are single-use. Only their digest is stored, they expire after 5 minutes to 24 hours, and they can be bound to an existing agent for re-enrollment (`internal/agents`, `migrations/000005_agent_identity.up.sql`).
- Settings → Management agents creates and revokes them (`components/remote/agents-settings.tsx`).
- An enrolled agent is immediately `active`.

## Changes
1. **Schema (new migration).** `agent_deployment_keys` stores: name, secret digest, Core key fingerprint, `max_uses`, `used_count`, expiry (up to 90 days), optional device tag or group to apply, `approval` mode (`manual` default, or `automatic`), and created/revoked fields. Add agent status `pending_approval`. Do not edit applied migrations.
2. **Token format.** `nerve-deploy-v1.<key id>.<secret>.<Core key fingerprint>`, so the agent pins Core's key exactly as it does today. `enroll` and `service install` accept it through the same file or environment paths.
3. **Enrollment.** Core checks the key (not revoked or expired, use count left) and creates a new agent per enrollment, atomically incrementing `used_count`. With `manual` approval the agent is `pending_approval`: it may heartbeat but receives no commands and is not associated with a device until approved.
4. **UI.** A deployment keys section to create (shown once), list with usage and revoke. A pending agents list with host facts and key fingerprint, and Approve / Reject actions. Audit every step.
5. Revoking a key never affects agents already approved.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Integration tests: use limit, expiry, revocation, concurrent enrollments do not exceed `max_uses`, pending agents get no commands, approve and reject are audited
- [ ] Single-use enrollment tokens keep working unchanged
- [ ] Pending state visible in the agent list; `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, browser check
- [ ] Security review; `REMOTE_MANAGEMENT.md`, `AGENT_SETUP.md` updated; CI green

tickets.title: Agent-initiated credential key rotation
tickets.body:
## Goal
An enrolled agent replaces its Ed25519 credential key through a signed, audited exchange with Core, without an operator creating a re-enrollment. Same agent ID, new key; the old credential is revoked.

## Current state (origin/master `f9c8b7f`)
- `agent_credentials` (`migrations/000005_agent_identity.up.sql`): immutable key material, one active credential per agent (`agent_credentials_one_active_idx`), final revocation, `revocation_reason IN ('revoked','reenrolled','removed')`.
- `agents.Repository.Authenticate` (`internal/agents/repository.go`) verifies signed headers, revocation, nonce replay and clock skew. Responses are Core-signed and verified against the pinned Core key (`cmd/nerve-agent/management.go`).
- The only rotation path today is operator re-enrollment (`nerve-agent enroll --force`, `docs/REMOTE_MANAGEMENT.md`). The identity file is written by `saveIdentity` (`cmd/nerve-agent/identity.go`).

## Changes
1. **Migration `000011`** (or the next free number): allow `revocation_reason = 'rotated'`. Do not edit `000005`.
2. **Endpoint** `POST /api/v1/agent/credential/rotate` behind `agentEndpoint`. The body carries the new public key and a proof-of-possession signature by the new key over agent ID, old credential ID, new public key and a timestamp. In one transaction Core inserts the new credential, revokes the old one as `rotated`, and writes an audit entry with `actor_agent_id`. It returns the new credential ID in a Core-signed response.
3. **Agent.** `nerve-agent rotate-key` plus automatic rotation after a configurable maximum key age (default off in this ticket). Crash safety: write the new key to a pending file first. Switch `identity.json` only after the Core-signed response is verified. On start with a pending file, try the new credential, fall back to the old one, and discard the pending key if Core does not know it. A running agent picks up the new identity without a restart (the existing identity poll).
4. **UI and docs.** The agent detail view shows the credential's age and the rotation history from the audit log. `REMOTE_MANAGEMENT.md` documents rotation and removes the "not implemented" note.

## Out of scope
Core signing-key rotation (separate ticket), key rotation for the discovery worker or sensor (K-9, K-14).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Rotation succeeds only with a valid old-key signature and a valid new-key proof; replays, revoked agents and duplicate keys are refused (integration tests against PostgreSQL)
- [ ] Old credential is revoked as `rotated`, the new one is the only active credential, and the change is audited
- [ ] Agent unit tests for the pending-key crash cases (Core committed but agent did not, and the reverse)
- [ ] Security review; `go test ./...`, `go vet` (Linux and `GOOS=windows`), integration tests and CI green; docs updated

tickets.title: Authenticate the Windows traffic sensor with a per-sensor enrolled identity
tickets.body:
## Goal
Replace the shared `NERVE_SENSOR_TOKEN` HMAC with a per-sensor identity that can be enrolled and revoked from Core.

## Current state (origin/master `f9c8b7f`)
- The sensor is a separate C#/.NET Windows service (`native/windows-sensor/Program.cs`) running as LocalService. It posts snapshots to a separate loopback-only Core listener (container port 8091, published as `127.0.0.1:${NERVE_SENSOR_PORT}`, not routed by Nginx).
- `internal/traffic/sensor.go` `SensorStore.ingest` checks HMAC-SHA256 over `unix_seconds\nnonce\nbody` with the shared token, a 30 s window and an in-memory nonce set. The store has no database access.
- `docs/WINDOWS_TRAFFIC_SENSOR.md` states that this does not protect against a local administrator or a process that can read the owner's `.env`.

## Decision needed first (decision record)
The .NET base class library has no Ed25519. Options:
1. Add an Ed25519 dependency to the sensor (for example NSec or BouncyCastle) and reuse the `agentproto` signed-header format and enrollment flow.
2. Have the sensor post to the local `nerve-agent`, which already holds an enrolled identity, and let the agent forward signed snapshots.
3. Keep HMAC but with a per-sensor secret issued at enrollment and revocable in Core, stored in the database.

The loopback-only listener already limits exposure, so record the threat model the change addresses before picking an option.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decision record under `docs/DECISIONS/` choosing one option and its threat model
- [ ] Sensor reports are authenticated per sensor and revocable; the shared token is deprecated with a migration path for existing installations (`setup.ps1`, `manage-traffic-sensor.ps1`)
- [ ] Tests for bad signatures, replay, revocation and the legacy path; `scripts/test-sensor.ps1` and `test-compose.ps1` still pass
- [ ] Security review; `WINDOWS_TRAFFIC_SENSOR.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` updated

notes.author: claude
notes.text:
Not started; two blockers.
1. The spec requires a maintainer decision first: options 1, 2 or 3. It is an architecture choice between real alternatives, so I did not pick one inside the work loop. Assessment for the decision: option 3 (per-sensor HMAC secret stored and revoked in Core) is the smallest change and needs no new .NET crypto dependency. Option 2 (forward through the local nerve-agent) reuses the enrolled identity and revocation, but couples the sensor to an agent install and moves the local authentication problem to the agent. Option 1 adds a .NET Ed25519 dependency (NSec or BouncyCastle).
2. Every option needs a migration (revocable per-sensor state) or touches the agent enrollment flow, which K-22 (PR #75, unmerged) is changing and which adds migration 000011. Added depends_on K-22.
To start it: record the chosen option on this card, and land K-22.

notes.author: claude
notes.text: Correction: a migration alone would not conflict with K-22, because the ledger is keyed by filename. The real blocker is the open maintainer decision between options 1–3 (option 2 would build on the agent enrollment K-22 changes). I kept depends_on K-22 only so the work loop does not pick the ticket up before that decision. Remove the dependency once the option is recorded here (immediately if you choose option 3).

tickets.title: Core signing key rotation without agent re-enrollment
tickets.body:
## Goal
An operator rotates `NERVE_CORE_SIGNING_KEY` while enrolled agents keep working, without re-enrolling them.

## Current state (origin/master `f9c8b7f`)
- Core signs every agent response with one Ed25519 key from `NERVE_CORE_SIGNING_KEY` (`internal/agentproto/core.go` `SignCoreResponse`, header `X-NERVE-Core-Key`). The agent pins exactly one Core public key in `identity.json` (`cmd/nerve-agent/identity.go`) and rejects any response signed by another key (`VerifyCoreResponse`).
- Enrollment tokens embed the Core key fingerprint (`nerve-enroll-v2`), so outstanding tokens stop working when the key changes.
- `docs/REMOTE_MANAGEMENT.md` says that changing the key requires re-enrolling every agent.

## Changes
1. Core accepts an optional `NERVE_CORE_NEXT_SIGNING_KEY`. While it is set, Core keeps signing with the current key and announces the next public key in signed heartbeat responses.
2. The agent stores the announced key as a second pinned key only when the announcement is signed by the currently pinned key. It then accepts responses signed by either key.
3. The operator promotes the next key to current (`setup.ps1` helper or documented `.env` edit). Core then signs with the new key. Agents that never saw the announcement fail closed with a clear diagnose message telling the operator to re-enroll them.
4. The agent list shows which Core key each agent has pinned, so the operator can see when it is safe to promote.
5. Outstanding enrollment tokens that pin the old key are rejected with a clear error. Document this.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Agents that received the announcement keep working across the switch; agents that did not fail closed with a diagnosable error (integration tests)
- [ ] A next key announced without a valid current-key signature is never pinned
- [ ] Agent list exposes the pinned Core key per agent
- [ ] Decision record for the two-key rollover; security review; `REMOTE_MANAGEMENT.md` updated; CI green

tickets.title: Approval gate for privileged commands: HTTPS, trusted devices, scopes, signed approvals
tickets.body:
## Goal
Core can queue a privileged command only when every policy precondition holds. The operator confirms with the target's identity and evidence in view, and the agent receives a Core-signed approval it can verify on its own. Still no privileged command type is enabled. This ticket builds the gate that K-3, K-5 and K-6 will use.

## Current state (master `f9c8b7f`)
- `internal/remote/policy.go`: `Policy{Type, Risk, Permission, timeouts, MaxOutputBytes, normalize}`. Only read-only types exist. `authz.RemoteExecutePrivileged` exists but is unused for queuing.
- `createCommand` (`internal/httpapi/commands.go`) checks the role permission and the policy, then queues.
- Device trust state (`unknown`/`reviewed`/`trusted`/`blocked`) is operator-owned (`internal/devices/metadata.go`). Agents are associated with devices.
- Core-signed responses (`internal/agentproto/core.go`) give authenticity, not confidentiality. Agents may talk to Core over plain HTTP today.

## Changes
1. **HTTPS requirement.** The agent reports its effective transport (an `https` API URL with verified TLS) in the signed heartbeat. Core stores it and refuses to queue privileged commands for an agent whose last heartbeat was not over verified HTTPS. The agent independently refuses privileged work when its own transport is not HTTPS.
2. **Trusted-device check.** Privileged commands need an agent associated with a device in the `trusted` state. A `blocked` device refuses all commands.
3. **Scopes.** New migration with `remote_scopes`: a role or user, a device or device tag, and the allowed command types. Seed it so admins keep their current behaviour. `createCommand` checks the scope for privileged types.
4. **Two-step confirmation.** `POST .../commands` for a privileged type creates the command in a new `awaiting_approval` state. It returns the target identity summary (device name, trust, agent fingerprint, association evidence). `POST /remote/commands/{id}/approve` by an operator holding the permission moves it to `queued` and stores a Core-signed approval envelope: command ID, type, parameter digest, agent ID, device ID and expiry. Approvals expire (default 10 minutes). Self-approval is allowed only when the policy says so; the default is yes, so a single admin can operate. Everything is audited.
5. **Agent verification.** The agent verifies the envelope against its pinned Core key before handing the command on. The privileged helper (K-2) verifies it again.
6. A `Policy.RequiresApproval` flag; all read-only policies keep `false`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Integration tests: each precondition (HTTPS, trusted device, scope, permission, approval expiry, approval for a different command or agent) is refused on its own, with a specific error code and an audit entry
- [ ] Envelope tests: tampered digest, wrong key, expired, replayed
- [ ] UI confirmation dialog shows target identity and evidence before approving
- [ ] Migration does not edit applied ones; security review; CI green

tickets.title: Authorized remote agent updates with verification and rollback
tickets.body:
## Goal
An operator updates an enrolled agent to a signed release from the UI. The update is verified, applied by the privileged helper, and rolled back automatically if the new agent does not come back healthy.

## Prerequisites
- K-7: signed release manifests and `internal/release` verification.
- K-2: privileged helper and local channel, plus the approval gate (K-17). The unprivileged agent cannot replace its own service binary.
- K-21: Core's verified release store and download routes, which the agent fetches updates from.

## Changes
1. **Command type** `agent.update`, with policy `RiskPrivileged` and approval required. Parameters: target version only. Core resolves the release from its release store (K-21) and refuses downgrades below the minimum Core version.
2. **Distribution.** The agent downloads the files from Core's download routes (K-21) and verifies manifest signature and artifact hashes before handing them to the helper.
3. **Helper apply.** Stage the new binary next to the old one, swap atomically, restart the service, and keep the previous binary. If the agent sends no signed heartbeat with the new version within a deadline (for example 2 minutes), restore the old binary, restart, and report `rolled_back` with the reason.
4. **UI.** Agent detail shows the current version, available releases and update history. The fleet list shows outdated agents.
5. **Audit.** Request, approval, apply, success or rollback.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Integration tests: unsigned or tampered release refused, downgrade refused, approval required
- [ ] End-to-end on Linux systemd: successful update, and forced rollback with a broken binary
- [ ] Windows: update and rollback verified on a real elevated host, or explicitly recorded as not verified
- [ ] Security review; `REMOTE_MANAGEMENT.md` and `AGENT_SETUP.md` updated; CI green

tickets.title: Core serves verified agent downloads and a one-line install command
tickets.body:
## Goal
An administrator installs the agent on any Windows or Linux endpoint with one pasted command, without a repository checkout or artifact folder. The endpoint downloads the agent from NERVE Core and verifies it before running it.

## Current state (master `f9c8b7f`, PR #73)
- Agent artifacts are built by `Dockerfile.agent --target artifact` (binary plus `install-windows.ps1` / `install-linux.sh`) and are not published anywhere.
- After PR #73, Settings → Management agents shows a PowerShell command that must run in the folder containing `install-windows.ps1` and `nerve-agent.exe`. The token reaches the agent through `NERVE_AGENT_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN`.
- K-7 adds signed release manifests (per-file SHA-256) and `internal/release` verification.

## Changes
1. **Release store in Core.** An operator imports a release from Settings, either by fetching a GitHub release or by uploading the artifacts. Core verifies the manifest signature with the pinned release key (`internal/release`) and refuses unsigned or tampered releases. It stores the files in a volume and marks one version as current. The web container never downloads anything on its own.
2. **Download routes.** `GET /api/v1/agent-downloads/{version}/{platform}/{file}`, routed through Nginx. These routes serve only verified files, are read-only, have no authentication (the files are not secret) and are rate limited. A `manifest.json` route gives the hashes.
3. **One-line install.** The token dialog generates a command per platform that:
   - downloads the installer and binary for the current version into a fresh temporary directory;
   - checks each SHA-256 against the value embedded in the copied command;
   - runs the installer with the API URL and the token in `NERVE_AGENT_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN`;
   - removes the temporary directory.

   Windows uses PowerShell 5.1 compatible commands (`Invoke-WebRequest`, `Get-FileHash`). Linux uses `curl` and `sha256sum` under `sudo`.
4. **HTTP is allowed, with a visible warning (maintainer decision).** Small test and development installs must work without HTTPS. Over plain HTTP the dialog still offers the one-line command, behind a warning that states the risk: anyone on the network path can replace the download, the expected hash and the token in transit. The recommendation is HTTPS for production. The command itself prints the same warning when the API URL is `http://`. Over HTTPS no warning is shown.
5. **Docs.** `AGENT_SETUP.md` describes production installation (HTTPS recommended) and test installation over HTTP; the folder-based command is kept for development.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Import refuses unsigned, tampered or wrong-key releases (tests); only verified files are served
- [ ] Generated commands fail closed on a hash mismatch, a missing download or a failed install, and always remove the temporary directory and the token variable (PowerShell 5.1 and bash tests against a stub server)
- [ ] Over plain HTTP the command is available with the warning in the UI and in the command output; over HTTPS without it
- [ ] End-to-end install on a clean Windows VM and a Linux systemd host, against both an HTTP and an HTTPS review stack
- [ ] Security review; `AGENT_SETUP.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` updated; CI green

notes.author: claude
notes.text: Blocked on K-22 (PR #75, unmerged). The one-line command goes into the token dialog in components/remote/agents-settings.tsx, which K-22 restructures for deployment keys. The download routes go into httpapi/server.go, which K-22 also changes. For rollout the command should accept a nerve-deploy-v1 key as well as a single-use token. Building this off master would mean redoing the dialog after K-22 lands. Note: the end-to-end criterion (clean Windows VM, HTTP and HTTPS stacks) needs the maintainer's hosts.

tickets.title: Windows MSI for GPO, Intune and SCCM rollout (no paid code signing)
tickets.body:
## Goal
IT rolls the agent out to many Windows PCs with standard tools: a Group Policy software installation, an Intune line-of-business app or SCCM. The package is an MSI that installs the service and enrolls with a deployment key passed at install time.

## Maintainer decision: no paid code-signing certificate
The project buys no Authenticode certificate. Integrity comes from the Ed25519-signed release manifest (K-7), which covers the MSI hash and is checked by Core on import (K-21). The project ships the MSI without an Authenticode signature. This has consequences:
- Installs pushed by GPO, Intune or SCCM run without user interaction and are not subject to the SmartScreen prompt for downloaded files. Opening a browser-downloaded MSI by hand does show the "unknown publisher" warning; document this.
- Organisations with their own PKI (for example AD CS) can sign the MSI with an internal code-signing certificate and trust it through the Trusted Publishers policy. Document the steps; the project does not depend on it.

## Prerequisites
- K-7: versioned, signed releases.
- K-21: Core serves verified downloads, so the MSI is published there.
- K-22: reusable deployment keys with approval, because one key must enroll many machines.

## Changes
1. **MSI build** with WiX v4 in the release workflow:
   - installs `nerve-agent.exe` to `%ProgramFiles%\NERVE\Agent` and runs the same `service install` logic as `install-windows.ps1`;
   - public properties `NERVE_API_URL`, `NERVE_DEPLOYMENT_KEY` (marked hidden, so it is not written to MSI logs) and `NERVE_CA_FILE`;
   - upgrade and uninstall without losing the identity, unless a purge property is set;
   - per-machine install, so it works for GPO assignment.
2. **Key handoff.** The deployment key reaches `service install` through the environment, never the command line. Document that a key in a GPO or Intune assignment is readable by administrators of those systems, so it must be revocable and limited (K-22).
3. **Release manifest.** The MSI is listed with its SHA-256 in the signed manifest (K-7). Core serves it only after verification (K-21).
4. **Docs.** `AGENT_SETUP.md` with GPO, Intune and SCCM recipes, how to check the MSI hash against the manifest, the SmartScreen behaviour, and optional signing with an internal certificate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Silent install `msiexec /i nerve-agent.msi /qn NERVE_API_URL=… NERVE_DEPLOYMENT_KEY=…` installs, enrolls into `pending_approval` and starts the service on a clean Windows VM; the key does not appear in the verbose MSI log
- [ ] Upgrade to a newer MSI keeps the identity; uninstall removes the service
- [ ] MSI hash is in the signed release manifest and Core refuses a modified MSI
- [ ] Security review; CI green
